question.leadin: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa paved the way for successful later sieges of Cordoba and Seville in this conflict.
question.text: Name this religious conflict between Christian states and Muslim states in the Iberian Peninsula, which is named for the reacquisition of traditionally Christian lands.
question.clue: The actions of El Cid handed the Almoravids their only defeat when trying to unite all the taifas during this period.

swap.text: This was the largest boat of the three in Columbus's fleet. It ran aground due to incompetent piloting and was dismantled to build the first Spanish settlement in the New World.
swap.clue: This ship, the largest and slowest of the three that Christopher Columbus used in his first voyage to the Americas.

question.leadin: This group was commanded by the Duke of Medina Sidonia after its initially designated leader, Alvaro de Bazan, died.
question.text: Name this massive naval fleet whose intended invasion of England failed.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Invincible Armada or Armada Invencible]
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.text: This confessor of Isabella also led the the Spanish Inquisition as the Grand Inquisitor.
swap.clue: This Dominican friar was the first Grand Inquisitor, becoming infamous for his zeal and cruelty.

question.leadin: Federico Garcia Lorca's assassination was likely carried out by forces loyal to this party, a journalist member of which, Eduardo Molina Fajardo, later investigated his death.
question.text: Name this party which became the sole legal party in Francoist Spain after the end of the Spanish Civil War.
question.answerHtml: Falange [or the Phalanx or Falange Española Tradicionalista y de las Juntas de Ofensiva Nacional Sindicalista or FET y de las JONS or Traditionalist Spanish Phalanx of the Councils of the National Syndicalist Offensive]
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.leadin: A White House on Puerto Rico was owned by this man, its first colonial governor.
swap.text: Name this explorer who apocryphally searched for the Fountain of Youth and discovered the Gulf Stream in 1513. While Governor of Hispaniola, he crushed a native Taino (TAY-noh) revolt.
swap.answerHtml: Juan Ponce de Leon [prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: Rumors of gold led him to establish the colony of Caparra, the first European settlement in Puerto Rico.

question.text: The captains of all five ships were killed before the completion of the Magellan Expedition. This man managed to complete the circumnavigation after taking over as captain of the Victoria.
question.clue: This man was promoted to lead one expedition after his predecessor was (+) killed at the Battle of Mactan.

swap.text: The war featured an alliance of Portugal, Great Britain, and the Holy Roman Empire, among others, who fought to keep this man, the nephew of Louis XIV of France
swap.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

question.text: He raised eyebrows in April 2004 when he promised "the beginning of complete equality of the sexes" and an "unceasing fight against criminal machismo" after being elected on an anti-Iraq war platform. For 15 points, name this Socialist prime minister of Spain.
question.clue: Shortly after the 2004 Madrid train bombings, this Socialist defeated Jose Aznar's Popular Party to become Prime Minister of Spain.

swap.leadin: The Islamic state based out of this city was established when Abd ar-Rahman I organized the remnants of Kulthum's garrison, who had been living there for a decade.
swap.text: Identify this seat of a caliphate whose illustrious Great Mosque was purchased from the Visigoths and reconverted to a church under Alfonso X.
swap.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the cartoon character John Bull.
question.text: Along with "Nicholas Frog" and "Lewis Baboon," John Bull first appeared in a pamphlet series criticizing this conflict. The Duke of Marlborough won the Battle of Blenheim during this conflict.
question.clue: The Treaty of Rastatt was signed during this conflict, after which the English were given control of the asiento.

swap.text: This daughter of Ferdinand and Isabella and wife of Phillip the Handsome was a Queen of Spain who suffered from mental illness and was forced to live in a nunnery for much of her reign.
swap.answerHtml: Joanna the Mad [or Juana la Loca; or Joanna of Castile; or Juana de Castilla]
swap.clue: After Charles was elected Holy Roman Emperor, the Comuneros rebellion in Spain tried to overthrow him in favor of this woman, his mother, who was confined for her alleged mental illness after the revolt was put down.

question.leadin: Identify the following monarchs with Spanish connections.
question.text: This king, in power from 1252 to 1284, founded universities at Salamanca and Toledo in addition to promoting Castilian as a scholarly language.
question.answerHtml: Alfonso X of Castile [or Alfonso the Wise or Alfonso el Sabio; accept translations similar to those above]
question.clue: It was for this king that Jehuda ben Moses Cohen and Isaac ben Sid assembled namesake astronomical tables.

swap.leadin: The initial letters of the sections of a law code from this kingdom form an acrostic of the name of the king that compiled it.
swap.text: Name this Spanish kingdom that united with Aragon after its queen Isabella married Ferdinand II.
swap.clue: Henry of Trast´amara took over this polity afer the death of its ruler Peter the Cruel in its civil war.

question.text: Along with their brother Leander, this bishop and patron saint of the internet was instrumental in eliminating Arianism from the Visigothic kingdom, and also found time to compile their encyclopaedic Etymologiae.
question.clue: This man wrote that Justinian was "admiring the heresy of Acefali" during the Three Chapters Controversy. This church father converted Reccared and standardized the use of several punctuation marks in one work.

swap.leadin: This campaign was legendarily brought on after a king opened 27 padlocks to enter a chamber and read a scroll, which prophesied that the horsemen painted on the walls would invade his kingdom.
swap.text: Describe this campaign that began with the defeat of King Roderic at an early 8th-century AD battle that was won by a Berber general.
swap.answerHtml: the Arab conquest of Spain [accept answers with Umayyad or Muslim or Tariq ibn Ziyad in place of “Arab”; accept the fall of the Visigothic Kingdom or clear equivalents; accept answers with synonyms for conquest or fall; accept the Battle of Guadalete or the Battle of 711; accept answers with Iberia or Hispania or Andalusia or al-Andalus or the Visigothic Kingdom in place of “Spain”]

question.text: This term is given to the petty Muslim kingdoms or emirates that sprung up on the Iberian Peninsula afer the fall of Umayyad-ruled Cordoba caliphate. These kingdoms ofen hired Christian mercenaries to battle rival states, and paid a tribute called parias to the Christian kingdoms.
question.clue: This kingdoms that included Seville, Granada, and Zaragoza whose fighting provided the opening for the conquest of several cities by their Christian neighbors.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early modern European cartography.
swap.text: In 1767, ambassador Ferdinando Galiani found a "treasure trove" of parchment maps produced earlier under the rule of this kingdom. Centuries earlier, mercenaries from this kingdom were led by Roger de Flor ("roo-ZHAY duh FLO").
swap.answerHtml: Aragon [or Reino d’Aragón or Regne d’Aragó; prompt on Naples by asking “under the rule of what kingdom?”]
swap.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

question.leadin: The Onacino and Gamboino clans fought during this conflict.
question.text: Name this conflict in medieval Spain between landowners called juanchos in which many dorretxeak were built.
question.answerHtml: The War of the Bands [accept Guerra de los Bandos; accept Bando Gerrak]

swap.leadin: Detailed city planning policies regarding presidios and pueblos were codified by this institution in a compilation of similarly named laws issued in 1573.
swap.text: Name this institution that compiled a massive survey into the Relaciones geograficas to inform its members. To address government abuses, this institution was restructured under the 1542 New Laws.
swap.answerHtml: Council of the Indies [or the Royal and Supreme Council of the Indies; accept Real y Supremo Consejo de las Indias]
